chapter: Early influences, Oliver date and trombone peers
title: Morris Brown band-mates and the first things he played
summary: No one else in the Morris Brown band turned professional; he describes the white teacher writing parts on the board.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Picking up the horn: first instrument and the trombone

blocks.x: You're talking to someone who does that all the time. Donald Byrd.
When you were younger and you were playing say at Morris Brown, could you name some of the other musicians that surrounded you in some of those early bands?
No one played in the band while I was there that never turned out professionally. Not one.
You were 14 years old when you went in there?
When you first started to play?
What were the first things that you happened to learn how to play?
I don't know. I just started blowing.

Blowing. I remember one night we had a white teacher and I still couldn't read but he would write on the board what he would want the trombone parts, you know, different parts to play. So, the first tune was Tuck Me to Sleep in My Old Kentucky Home. I remember the first eight bars after this many and that's as far as I went (sings the eight bars) and that was the big show MM. I'm not kiddin'. (inaudible) he wouldn't let no trombone I kept take it out ... we had about four trombones and played Bugle call and let every boy I was a kid and didn't know take a group called Rag. Everybody that was a big my better, I'd just go ahead and do my best and leave the shot ... (inaudible) rest.
